name: Grip
summary: How you hold the bat. A relaxed, neutral grip lets you play both wings without changing your hand.

name: Ready position
summary: The athletic stance you return to after every shot: feet wide, knees bent, weight forward, bat in front.

name: Ball feel
summary: Soft hands and a feel for the ball on the bat. The base for touch, spin and control.

name: Basic footwork
summary: Small side steps, the cross-over step and the pivot, so you hit every ball from a balanced position.

name: Forehand drive
summary: The first attacking stroke: a short, compact topspin hit on the forehand side.

name: Backhand drive
summary: A compact topspin hit in front of the body on the backhand side.

name: Backhand push
summary: A short backspin return against backspin. Keeps the ball low and safe.

name: Forehand push
summary: The forehand version of the push: a controlled backspin return.

name: Forehand loop against backspin
summary: Lift a backspin ball with an upward brushing swing. The main way to start an attack.

name: Serving
summary: Legal serves with clear spin and controlled length, so you start the point on your terms.

name: Receiving
summary: Read the serve's spin and length, then return it safely or attack it.

name: Serve and third-ball attack
summary: Serve so the return is predictable, then attack the third ball on purpose.

name: Table tennis fitness
summary: Warm-ups, quick legs, a strong core and healthy shoulders and wrists.

name: Focus and routines
summary: A short routine before each point, breathing to reset, and calm under pressure.
